title: Evaluating New LinkedIn Labor Market Tightness Indicators - Liberty Street Economics
gist: NY Fed researchers test three LinkedIn labor-tightness indicators against JOLTS V/U and find the Jobs per Jobseeker Index (correlation 0.733 with V/U) has the lowest nowcast and forecast error for both CPI and ECI inflation, while the LinkedIn Hiring Rate also beats V/U in forecasting. The indicators arrive about a week after month-end versus a five-week JOLTS lag, though they cover only LinkedIn-posted jobs.

insights.claim: The Jobs per Application Index (JPAI) is LinkedIn's count of 'attractive' job openings (paid-promoted or manually listed, and receiving at least one application in the local labor market) divided by total job applications submitted on LinkedIn.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth B. Li
insights.so_what: Defines a demand-over-applications tightness gauge that is exposed to application-volume noise such as mass Easy Apply behavior.
insights.quote: The JPAI is defined as the number of attractive job openings in a given month divided by the number of job applications submitted on LinkedIn.
insights.locator: How Are the New LinkedIn Measures Constructed?

insights.claim: The Jobs per Jobseeker Index (JPJI) divides attractive openings by the number of distinct jobseekers who submitted at least one application that month, so it normalizes by people rather than applications, closely mirroring the vacancies-to-unemployment logic.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth B. Li
insights.so_what: Counting people rather than applications is plausibly why JPJI beats JPAI in the tests.
insights.quote: The JPJI is defined as the number of attractive job openings that month divided by the number of jobseekers that submitted at least one job application on LinkedIn that month.
insights.locator: How Are the New LinkedIn Measures Constructed?

insights.claim: The LinkedIn Hiring Rate (LHR) is the share of LinkedIn members who added a new employer to their profile, indexed to the average month of 2016 (1.05 means 5% above), and is used seasonally adjusted.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth B. Li
insights.so_what: A profile-update based hiring proxy that is available well before official hires data.
insights.quote: This number is indexed to the average month in 2016; for example, an index of 1.05 indicates a hiring rate that is 5 percent higher than the average month in 2016.
insights.locator: How Are the New LinkedIn Measures Constructed?

insights.claim: All three LinkedIn measures can be published within about a week of month-end (August 2026 data in early September) versus roughly a five-week lag for JOLTS, giving a real-time edge on labor market tightness.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth B. Li
insights.so_what: Timeliness is the core value: these indicators can move rate and wage-inflation expectations weeks before official JOLTS prints.
insights.quote: data for August 2026 could be made available in the first week of September, much sooner than JOLTS data which are available with about a five-week lag.
insights.locator: How Are the New LinkedIn Measures Constructed?

insights.claim: The measures are not representative of the whole US economy because they capture only jobs posted and applied to on LinkedIn, which skews toward white-collar and professional roles; the authors flag this as the key caveat.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth B. Li
insights.so_what: Sector skew could distort signals when white-collar and blue-collar labor markets diverge, for example during AI-driven white-collar hiring changes.
insights.quote: these measures are not necessarily representative of the U.S. economy as a whole, since they capture only jobs posted and applied to on LinkedIn
insights.locator: How Are the New LinkedIn Measures Constructed?

insights.claim: The JPJI tracks the JOLTS vacancies-to-unemployment (V/U) ratio with a 0.733 correlation over July 2019 to April 2026; it ran slightly above V/U just after COVID and slightly below from late 2022 to mid-2024.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth B. Li
insights.so_what: The JPJI is a credible high-frequency stand-in for V/U, though it understated tightness in 2022-24 relative to V/U.
insights.quote: The correlation between the two measures is 0.733.

insights.claim: The text reports a 0.95 correlation between the normalized LHR and the JOLTS hires rate when the sample starts in 2021 (excluding COVID onset swings), but the chart panel as rendered shows 'Correlation = 0.399', a discrepancy within the post (likely the full-sample figure).
insights.speaker: Elizabeth B. Li
insights.so_what: The LHR-hires link is strong only after removing COVID-era distortion; treat the headline 0.95 with care.
insights.quote: the correlation between the two (normalized) variables is 0.95.

insights.claim: The V/U ratio, vacancies from JOLTS divided by unemployed persons, is the benchmark tightness measure, and the study sample (July 2019 to April 2026) is limited by short JPJI and JPAI histories.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth B. Li
insights.so_what: A short sample that includes the COVID shock means results may not generalize across regimes.
insights.quote: we restrict attention to the period starting in July 2019 (given limited historical data availability for the JPJI and the JPAI) and ending in April 2026.

insights.claim: In real-time nowcasts of monthly CPI and quarterly ECI inflation, the JPJI has the lowest error and beats V/U for both price and wage inflation.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth B. Li
insights.so_what: A LinkedIn-derived gauge outperforms the standard official-data tightness measure at nowcasting inflation, a usable input for wage-inflation tracking before ECI prints.
insights.quote: The JPJI has the lowest nowcasting error, performing better than V/U in predicting both price and wage inflation.
insights.locator: How Good Are the New Measures for Nowcasting and Forecasting?

insights.claim: The LHR nowcasts CPI better than V/U but ECI worse than V/U, so its usefulness is asymmetric across price versus wage inflation.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth B. Li
insights.so_what: The LHR is more useful for goods and services price nowcasting than for wage-cost nowcasting.
insights.quote: The LHR performs better than V/U for CPI but worse for ECI.
insights.locator: How Good Are the New Measures for Nowcasting and Forecasting?

insights.claim: The JPAI and the JOLTS hires rate consistently nowcast worse than V/U, so the JOLTS hires rate is not a better tightness gauge despite being official data.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth B. Li
insights.so_what: Official-source status does not guarantee predictive power; hires-based official measures lag the vacancy ratio.
insights.quote: The JPAI and the JOLTS hires rate are consistently worse than V/U.
insights.locator: How Good Are the New Measures for Nowcasting and Forecasting?

insights.claim: The nowcast method runs rolling regressions of inflation through t-1 on tightness measures and predicts period t using tightness through t, scoring by average RMSE relative to V/U set to 100.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth B. Li
insights.so_what: The evaluation is pseudo real-time but only a single-benchmark RMSE comparison, with no significance tests reported.
insights.quote: In practice, we run rolling regressions of inflation up to period t-1 (the last period official data are available) on LMT measures.
insights.locator: How Good Are the New Measures for Nowcasting and Forecasting?

insights.claim: One-step-ahead forecasts of CPI and ECI inflation also favor the JPJI, which has lower error than V/U for both price and wage inflation.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth B. Li
insights.so_what: A single timely index carries forward-looking information on wage and price pressure, relevant to Fed rate-path calibration.
insights.quote: the JPJI is the best performing measure, with a lower forecasting error than V/U in predicting both price and wage inflation.
insights.locator: How Good Are the New Measures for Nowcasting and Forecasting?

insights.claim: In forecasting, the LHR beats V/U for both CPI and ECI though it trails the JPJI, a better showing than in nowcasting.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth B. Li
insights.so_what: Hiring-rate signals appear to lead inflation, adding some value as a leading indicator.
insights.quote: the LHR also performs better than V/U in predicting both inflation measures, though still worse than the JPJI.
insights.locator: How Good Are the New Measures for Nowcasting and Forecasting?

insights.claim: The JPAI and the JOLTS hires rate are the worst forecasters, though the JPAI beats V/U for ECI forecasting.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth B. Li
insights.so_what: The JPAI has marginal wage-forecast value but is not a reliable standalone gauge.
insights.quote: the JPAI and the JOLTS hires rate are the worst-performing measures, though the JPAI performs better than V/U in forecasting ECI inflation.
insights.locator: How Good Are the New Measures for Nowcasting and Forecasting?

insights.claim: Good labor market tightness measures matter because tight markets imply stronger wage pressure, and thus feed predictions of wage inflation and calibration of monetary policy.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth B. Li
entities: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
insights.so_what: Tightness readings are a transmission link from labor data to inflation to rate decisions.
insights.quote: The labor market is considered tight if there are few job seekers available relative to job openings, implying stronger wage pressures as employers compete for scarce job seekers.

insights.claim: The NY Fed concludes that the JPJI and LHR track existing tightness measures and have RMSE comparable to or better than V/U, while being timelier, which makes them candidate additions to the real-time labor dashboard.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth B. Li
insights.so_what: Expect private platform data such as LinkedIn to gain weight in Fed and market labor nowcasts, a positioning edge for those tracking them before JOLTS.
insights.quote: these measures are also timelier than the JOLTS hires rate and traditional measures of tightness, such as V/U.

insights.claim: Because the evidence rests on about seven years including COVID, a pure RMSE ranking and one platform's user base, the JPJI's edge is suggestive rather than proven, and it could fade out of sample or under changing LinkedIn user behavior.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth B. Li
insights.so_what: Use these indicators as a complement to JOLTS and V/U, not a replacement, until a longer track record exists.
